# Labour Party Manifesto 2005: Summary

## Overview and Vision

The 2005 Labour manifesto, titled "Britain forward, not back," outlined New Labour's vision for a third term focused on providing opportunity and security for all in a changing world. Tony Blair presented the party's record since 1997 as proof of competence in managing the economy, reducing crime, and reforming public services, while pledging to build on these foundations.

## Record Since 1997

Labour highlighted significant achievements including:
- Creating the lowest unemployment in 30 years with two million more people in work
- Reducing child and pensioner poverty (two million fewer children and nearly two million fewer pensioners in absolute poverty)
- Reducing crime by 30 percent and adding nearly 13,000 police officers
- Doubling NHS spending, adding 79,000 nurses and 27,000 doctors
- Investing an extra £1,000 per pupil annually in education
- Helping over 500,000 young people into work through the New Deal

## Economic Policy

Labour pledged to maintain economic stability through the Bank of England framework, keeping inflation at two percent and adhering to fiscal rules of only borrowing to invest. They committed to not raising basic or top income tax rates and to implementing efficiency savings of £21 billion. The goal was full employment across all regions, raising the employment rate to 80 percent and increasing the minimum wage to £5.35 by October 2006.

## Education Reform

The manifesto emphasized "personalised learning" with plans to make every secondary school an independent specialist school. Key commitments included extending free nursery provision, improving primary literacy and numeracy, establishing 200 Academies by 2010, and raising apprenticeship quality. Higher education would see continued expansion toward 50 percent participation by 2010, with fees capped at £3,000.

## Healthcare

The NHS vision was "free to all, personal to each." Labour promised maximum 18-week waits from referral to treatment by 2008, free choice of hospital, expansion of NHS Foundation Trusts, and new community hospitals. Public health initiatives included restricting smoking in enclosed public places and improving school meals.

## Crime and Security

Pledges included neighborhood policing teams for every community, 24,000 Community Support Officers, expanded drug testing and treatment programs, and introduction of identity cards. Immigration would be controlled through a points-based system, with stronger border security measures.

## Family and Social Policy

Labour committed to ending child poverty by halving it by 2010-11, extending paid maternity leave to nine months by 2007, creating 3,500 Sure Start Children's Centres by 2010, and increasing homeownership by two million. Universal childcare for ages 3-14 would be delivered through extended schools.

## International Affairs

Britain would remain at the heart of Europe, supporting the Constitutional Treaty through referendum. The manifesto committed to reaching 0.7 percent of national income in development aid by 2013, using the G8 presidency to address climate change and African poverty, and maintaining strong armed forces while supporting the independent nuclear deterrent.

## Constitutional Reform

Plans included completing House of Lords reform, devolving more power to local authorities and neighborhoods, introducing directly elected mayors, and continuing devolution in Wales and London. Labour committed to restoring Northern Ireland's devolved institutions and maintaining the Human Rights Act while establishing a Commission on Equality and Human Rights.
